headline: Equinor is fighting an ongoing cyberattack; the US outage wave is still not linked to any attack

items.action: Energy-sector partners should review connections to Equinor systems and watch for follow-up statements.
items.title: Equinor detects ongoing cyberattack on IT systems
items.why: A major European energy supplier is under active attack, though production and data are reported unaffected.

items.action: Apply Check Point's emergency hotfixes now and check gateways for signs of compromise since October 30.
items.title: Check Point gateways are being wiped in PHP2Shell attacks
items.why: Attackers gain root on unpatched gateways and deploy destructive wipers.

items.action: Update the ScreenConnect technician client to 26.6.5 or later and disable third-party extensions.
items.title: ScreenConnect attacks spread from customers to MSP technicians
items.why: A worm-like toolkit turns one unpatched remote-support system into a route into many networks.

items.action: If you run Optimizely Web Experimentation, review your snippets; if you paid by card or sent crypto on an affected site that day, check the transaction.
items.title: Optimizely script injection reached 178 organizations' websites
items.why: Visitors to well-known sites on November 16 were served card-skimming and crypto-stealing code.

items.action: Warn staff that Microsoft will not email them threatening to delete held messages; report such emails.
items.title: Phishing emails exploit the Microsoft 365 outage
items.why: Messages cite the real incident number to look genuine.

items.title: NSA's classified network outage attributed to maintenance
items.why: It is the latest in a week of US outages; the agency reports no evidence of an attack.

plain_summary: The confirmed attacks today are on Norway's Equinor, whose production is unaffected, and on websites using Optimizely, where visitors were exposed to card-stealing code. The run of US outages (Microsoft, FAA, banks, NSA, Apple) is unsettling, but every organization gives a non-cyber cause and officials say it was not coordinated. Most people need to do nothing beyond watching for scam emails that exploit the outages. IT teams have several urgent patches.
